a: King of Qinghe; later King of Zhongshan

claims.dateText: Guisi after Huanglong 1/12; Emperor Xuan's death

title.en: Attendant at the Palace and Commandant of the Gentlemen

claims.note: Qinghe king later titled King of Zhongshan

title.en: Cavalry Commandant / Protector of the Western Regions

translationRepairs: Enfeoffed the Palace Attendant Xu Jia, uterine younger brother of the emperor's maternal grandfather, Marquis Dai of Ping'en, as Marquis of Ping'en to continue Marquis Dai's line.
Enfeoffed Xu Jia, Palace Regular Attendant and son of a full younger brother of the emperor's maternal grandfather, Marquis Dai of Ping'en, as Marquis of Ping'en to continue Marquis Dai's line.
同產弟子 is the son of a full younger brother, not the younger brother himself; the revision also uses the established rendering of 中常侍.
Jia Guanyin, an Awaiting Edict, argued that Zhujia should be abandoned to relieve the people's famine and distress.
Jia Juanzhi, an Awaiting Edict, argued that Zhuya should be abandoned to relieve the people's famine and distress.
賈捐之 is Jia Juanzhi, not Jia Guanyin, and 珠崖 is Zhuya; both corrections restore the Chinese and align with the prior unit's Zhuya.
Jia Guanyin, an Awaiting Edict, argued that Zhujia should be abandoned to relieve the people's famine and distress.
Awaiting Edict Jia Juanzhi considered it appropriate to abandon Zhuya, to save the people from famine.
The literal likewise misreads 賈捐之 as Jia Guanyin and 珠崖 as Zhujia; the replacement restores Jia Juanzhi, Zhuya, and 以為宜棄／救民饑饉.
On the last day of the fourth month of summer, which fell on Yiyou, the white crane pavilion at Maoling suffered a disaster.
On the last day of the fourth month of summer, which fell on Yiwei, the white crane pavilion at Maoling suffered a disaster.
乙未 is the sexagenary day Yiwei; Yiyou would be 乙酉, so the original day name is wrong.
In the first month of spring in the fifth year, Zhouzi Nanjun was made Zhou Chenghou Marquis, his position ranking after the feudal kings.
In the first month of spring in the fifth year, Lord Zhouzinan was made Marquis of Zhou Chengxiu, ranking immediately below the kings.
周子南君 is the title Lord of Zhouzinan, and 周承休侯 is Marquis of Chengxiu of Zhou; 'Zhouzi Nanjun' and 'Zhou Chenghou Marquis' misparse both titles.
In the third month, Crown Prince Kang was established as King of Jiyang.
In the third month, the emperor's son Kang was made King of Jiyang.
皇子 means the emperor's son; Crown Prince would be 皇太子, which the Chinese does not say.
In the sixth month, Crown Prince Xing was established as King of Xindu.
In the sixth month, the emperor's son Xing was made King of Xindu.
皇子 means the emperor's son; Crown Prince would be 皇太子, which the Chinese does not say.
Young and good Confucianism, and ascended position, summoned used Confucian scholars, entrusted them with government, Gong, Xue, Wei, Kuang alternately became chancellors.
From youth he loved Confucianism; when he ascended the throne, he summoned and employed Confucian scholars and entrusted government to them; Gong, Xue, Wei, and Kuang became chancellors in turn.
The original literal is ungrammatical and obscures 少而好儒、及即位、徵用儒生、委之以政、迭為宰相; the proposed English accurately restores that sequence.
Enfeoffed the Palace Attendant Xu Jia, uterine younger brother of the maternal grandfather, Marquis Dai of Ping'en, as Marquis of Ping'en to continue Marquis Dai's line.
Enfeoffed Xu Jia, Palace Regular Attendant and son of a full younger brother of the maternal grandfather, Marquis Dai of Ping'en, as Marquis of Ping'en to continue Marquis Dai's line.
同產弟子 identifies Xu Jia as the son of the maternal grandfather's full younger brother, and 中常侍 is Palace Regular Attendant.
Summer fourth month Yiyou last day, Maoling white crane pavilion disaster.
On the last day of the fourth month of summer, an Yiwei day, the White Crane Lodge at Maoling burned.
乙未 is Yiwei, not Yiyou, and 災 here records that the lodge burned.
Fifth year spring first month, used Zhou son Nanjun as Zhou Chenghou Marquis, position ranked feudal lords kings.
In the first month of spring in the fifth year, Lord Zhouzinan was made Marquis of Zhou Chengxiu, his rank immediately below the kings.
The original misparsed 周子南君 and 周承休侯 and left the rank clause ungrammatical.
Third month, established crown prince Kang as Jiyang King.
In the third month, the emperor's son Kang was made King of Jiyang.
皇子 means the emperor's son, not Crown Prince.
Sixth month, established crown prince Xing as Xindu King.
In the sixth month, the emperor's son Xing was made King of Xindu.
皇子 means the emperor's son, not Crown Prince.
